title: Bank telemarketing: cap the calls?
subtitle: Real campaign data, nothing planted. Does every extra call hurt?
question: Does each additional contact call to the same customer in a campaign reduce the chance that the customer subscribes to a term deposit?

decision_rule.metric: odds ratio of subscribing per additional contact call in the campaign

story: 45,211 customer records from phone campaigns of a Portuguese bank. A plain analysis says more calls to the same person means fewer subscriptions, so cap them. But who gets called many times is not random: hard-to-reach customers, the month, the contact channel and earlier campaigns all differ. Observational data, no planted effect; a live run only.

column_notes.age: age of the customer in years
column_notes.job: type of job of the customer; has missing values
column_notes.education: education level of the customer; has missing values
column_notes.default: whether the customer has credit in default
column_notes.balance: average yearly balance of the customer in euros
column_notes.housing: whether the customer has a housing loan
column_notes.loan: whether the customer has a personal loan
column_notes.contact: contact communication type of the last contact (cellular or telephone); has missing values
column_notes.day_of_week: despite its name, the day of the month of the last contact
column_notes.duration: duration of the last call in seconds; only known after the call, so post-treatment for this question
column_notes.campaign: number of contacts to this customer during this campaign, including the last one; the exposure of interest
column_notes.pdays: days since the customer was last contacted in a previous campaign; -1 means never contacted before
column_notes.previous: number of contacts before this campaign
column_notes.poutcome: outcome of the previous campaign; has missing values
column_notes.y: 1 if the customer subscribed to a term deposit, else 0; the outcome
